subject.title: Add an FxTwitter read transport for public lookups, threads, profiles, and search

question: Should Birdclaw adopt FxTwitter as an in-core, explicitly selected public-read provider, including support for user-configured self-hosted endpoints?
rationale: Source inspection shows a feasible implementation boundary, but code cannot decide whether Birdclaw should assume the provider's maintenance burden or what network destinations and disclosure policy the configurable endpoint may permit.

options.title: Approve a constrained provider
options.body: Implement a narrow public-read-only MVP through existing transport and ingestion boundaries, with explicit selection, capability errors, privacy disclosure, and a reviewed endpoint-security policy.

options.title: Limit the endpoint surface
options.body: Support only the public FxTwitter service initially and defer arbitrary self-hosted base URLs until the network trust model is defined.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Keep Birdclaw focused on its current authenticated transports and leave FxTwitter access to external tooling or a future extension boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve a constrained provider
recommendation.body: Implement a narrow public-read-only MVP through existing transport and ingestion boundaries, with explicit selection, capability errors, privacy disclosure, and a reviewed endpoint-security policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes Birdclaw's supported provider matrix, privacy posture, configuration surface, and long-term product maintenance commitment.
